title: Weight varies as the cube of length; a change in k means a change of form
look_for_in_this_kingdom: stem, trunk and shoot biomass against height or diameter; allometry databases (BAAD, Tallo, GlobAllomeTree), seed and leaf mass vs dimension
variables_needed: body or organism mass and length per individual or species
reported exponent b and condition factor k

claims.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
claims.statement: Whatever the law of increase in a linear dimension, volume and therefore weight tend to vary as the cube of linear dimensions, which mainly (though not wholly) explains why the human weight curve differs in shape from the stature curve.
claims.quote: whatever be the law of increment in a linear dimension, the law of increase in volume, and therefore in weight, will be that these latter magnitudes tend to vary as the cubes of the linear dimensions.

assessor_named_datasets.name: CDC National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey

claims.label: Changes in the length-weight constant k reveal changes of form during growth
claims.statement: Weight varies as the cube of length (W = kL³) in an animal of unchanging form and density, so tracking whether k stays constant or varies with length shows whether the animal's general form changes as it grows; such changes are likely as long as growth continues.
claims.quote: then the value of _k_, according to whether it varies or remains constant, will tell us at once whether there has or has not been a tendency to gradual alteration in the general form.

other_kingdoms_hint.animals: length-weight relationships (FishBase LWR, bird and mammal body-mass tables, AnAge, PanTHERIA, Amniote database), growth series with measured L and W
other_kingdoms_hint.fossils: body-mass estimates from fossil length (dinosaur, fish, mammal compilations), measured fossil lengths with mass proxies, volumetric reconstructions
